prompt: My custom SKMTC generator composes with a peer operation generator: in my Projection constructor I call this.insertOperation(PeerProjection, operation). For a handful of operations, generate now throws from inside the insert — the peer rejects the operation as unsupported (its capability gate) — and those items are recorded as errors in the manifest while the rest of the run completes. The peer's isSupported wants a JSON object request body and these operations have none. I'm thinking of wrapping the insertOperation call in a try/catch and falling back to emitting the type inline as a string so every item goes green. What's going on, and is the fallback OK?

criteria.check: Did the response explain that cross-generator insertOperation enforces the PEER's static isSupported (an unsupported operation throws at the Driver, the calling item is recorded as error, and the run continues) — loud, isolated failure by design?

Did the response direct the caller to gate on the peer's capability BEFORE inserting — e.g. mirror the peer's isSupported predicate in the caller's own isSupported / transform filter (or call PeerProjection's static isSupported) so unsupported operations never reach the insert?
Did the response reject the try/catch-plus-inline-string fallback (it silently produces a different artifact shape and hides the capability mismatch from the manifest)?
